title: Short Stirling LK238 Memorial, Gording
memorial_details: Stone and plaque at Gording. A photograph of P/O Ross Philp (the only crew member killed) is displayed inside Gording church. A Danish cross marks the original burial site near the crash location.
crew_summary: 1 killed (P/O Ross Philp, buried Gording Cemetery); 3 evaded to Sweden (Flower, Gee, Moloney, Woodham); 2 captured as POW (Abecassis, Walker). Pilot S/Ldr Abecassis evaded initially but was later captured and held at Stalag Luft III.
narrative:
On the evening of 6 October 1944, Short Stirling LK238 MA-X of 161 (Special Duties) Squadron departed RAF Tempsford at 22:29 on OP TABLEJAM 26, a clandestine SOE stores drop mission to occupied Denmark. 161 Squadron was one of the two RAF squadrons dedicated to covert operations supporting resistance movements across occupied Europe, flying agents and supplies in the dark.

At 01:26 on 7 October, as the Stirling flew near Holstebro in western Denmark, it was intercepted by Hauptmann Johann Dreher of 6./NJG3. Dreher shot the aircraft down — his third confirmed Abschuss. The crew's fates diverged dramatically. Squadron Leader G.E. Abecassis DFC, the pilot, initially evaded but was eventually captured and became a prisoner of war at Stalag Luft III. Flight Lieutenant Richard Gee (Navigator), Pilot Officer Lesley Flower (Flight Engineer), Pilot Officer Patrick Moloney (Air Gunner), and Flight Officer Samuel Woodham (Air Gunner) all successfully evaded and made it to neutral Sweden. Flight Officer K.H. Walker (Wireless Op) was captured and also became a POW.

Only one man was killed: P/O Ross F. Philp (RAAF), the Bombardier. He was buried locally at Gording Cemetery. His photograph is displayed in Gording church — an act of community remembrance that has kept his memory present in the village for more than 80 years.

The story of Hauptmann Dreher has a grim postscript. On 3 March 1945, during Unternehmen Gisela — the Luftwaffe's audacious retaliatory intruder operation against RAF Bomber Command airfields — Dreher was killed at Dunnington, North Yorkshire. The hunter who shot down LK238 over Denmark died less than five months later in the English night.

Searcher Søren Flensted, who documented this crash and many others across Denmark and whose photographs have preserved the memorial record, passed away in June 2025. His work underpins much of what is known about this loss.

crew.name: G.E. Abecassis
crew.fate_detail: Evaded initially after the crash but was subsequently captured. Held at Stalag Luft III.

crew.name: Ross F. Philp
crew.fate_detail: Killed when LK238 was shot down. Buried Gording Cemetery. Photograph displayed in Gording church.

crew.name: K.H. Walker
crew.fate_detail: Captured. Became a prisoner of war.

external_narratives.summary: Søren Flensted's definitive Danish aviation crash research, documenting the loss of LK238 near Holstebro, the NJG3 interception by Hauptmann Dreher, and the crew fates. Flensted died in June 2025; his records are the primary Danish source for this crash.
